goals: invite readiness-based access without false scarcity
sequence_strategy.timing: Five emails over two weeks before an evidence-gated launch; launch date remains a placeholder until approved.

emails.name: Finite games end

subject_lines.primary: Some work should end. The company should not.
subject_lines.benefit: Finish the task without losing continuity
subject_lines.urgency: No rush: start with the game you are actually playing

emails.preview_text: The organs are finite. The operator is not.
emails.hook: A useful agent knows when its task is finished.
emails.body:
A brand run should converge. A build should ship. A campaign should close.

The mistake is asking any one of those finite systems to become the company.

Cambium begins one level higher. It keeps the vision, current mission, viability bounds, and learning alive while specialist runs start, finish, and rest.

Over the next two weeks, we will show the model without asking you to believe a synthetic-founder story.
emails.ps: P.S. These emails are education drafts, not evidence that the product is publicly available.

emails.name: The continuity tax

subject_lines.primary: The company stops when you stop
subject_lines.curiosity: What only the founder is carrying
subject_lines.benefit: Reduce supervision without losing the thread
subject_lines.urgency: Name the continuity gap before adding another agent

emails.preview_text: More tools do not remove the founder as the only memory layer.
emails.hook: The hidden operating cost is not the task. It is the thread between tasks.
emails.body:
Founders pay a continuity tax every time they reconstruct context, check whether work really happened, reconcile conflicting outputs, or remember which constraint made an earlier decision safe.

More agents can increase that tax.

Cambium treats the venture as typed world-state with explicit bounds and replayable events. The aim is not less human judgment. It is less human reassembly.
emails.ps: P.S. If a system cannot show its source and authority, the founder still has to carry both.

emails.name: The viability worksheet

subject_lines.primary: A small worksheet for staying in the game
subject_lines.benefit: Turn risk into a named operating bound
subject_lines.urgency: Use the actual margin—not a countdown

emails.preview_text: Four questions: bound, signal, safe direction, authority.
emails.hook: Write down the one condition that would force your venture to stop.
emails.body:
1. What bound cannot be crossed?
2. What fresh evidence tells you the margin is narrowing?
3. Which reversible finite game could widen it?
4. Which authority is required before that game creates consequence?

That is the smallest useful Cambium loop. No 1024-dimensional dashboard required.

A bound you can name and verify is better than an impressive model you cannot govern.
emails.ps: P.S. Treat the worksheet as a hypothesis. The receipt should show when reality refutes it.

emails.name: Proof has a label

subject_lines.curiosity: Five labels that make claims safer
subject_lines.benefit: Know what is live before you trust it
subject_lines.urgency: Check the label before the claim travels

emails.hook: A beautiful diagram can still be only doctrine.
emails.body:
Cambium uses five plain labels.

Doctrine describes the intended system. Local means a source or test exists here. Production means the live boundary was probed. Held means the work exists but lacks authority or acceptance. Retired means the path is historical evidence, not a current option.

The label does not make a claim true. It makes the kind of truth visible.
emails.ps: P.S. No testimonial belongs in this sequence until a real person approves an exact quote and context.

emails.name: Ready when the gates are
emails.send_timing: When launch readiness is actually approved

subject_lines.primary: Cambium opens when the evidence is ready
subject_lines.curiosity: What must pass before the first garden opens
subject_lines.benefit: Begin with a governed first mapping
subject_lines.urgency: No artificial deadline—the readiness gate is the deadline

emails.preview_text: One venture. One bound. One event. One replay.
emails.hook: We will not turn a date into proof.
emails.body:
When the first product boundary is accepted, Cambium will open with one deliberately small experience: map a venture, name a bound, admit one event, and replay one decision.

If those four things are not legible, more autonomy would only hide the gap.

If you want to take part, join the readiness list. We will write again only when the product, policy, and evidence gates say the same thing.
emails.ps: P.S. Replace this placeholder only after consent handling, availability, and the first-wake acceptance receipt are real.
